text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- U.S. House of Representatives votes to renew China's normal trading status for another year.
- Singapore offers to share its experience in environmental protection with developing countries, and manages to attract interest of several countries within hours of announcing offer.
- Woman's teenage grandaughter and her boyfriend use grandmother's credit card for Singapore $35,000 shopping spree.

- Senior telecommunications executives now earn up to 40 percent more than counterparts in computer industry and could soon overtake those in financial sector to become most highly paid workers around.
- Pepsico Foods president for Asia-Pacific Ramesh Vangal quitting American beverage and snack food giant to set up US$200 million Asian food multinational.
- Thailand spent about US$5 billion shoring up currency last month, driving foreign exchange reserves to lowest in more than two years, economists say.
- Prospect of property buying spree in Taiwan by Hong Kong "red chips" sparks concern Beijing could be eyeing greater influence in Taipei to force early reunification.
- Hong Kong stocks surge 174.06 points, or 1.17 percent, as investors officials and business community welcome U.S. Congress decision to renew China's trading rights for another year.
- Infrastructure-based Van der Horst rebounds strongly after company reassures investors its poor first-half performance was "one-off" problem and second half will be better.
- Share price of automotive parts dealer Tye Soon jumps 10 percent to new high of 53.5 Singapore cents, bringing premium over offer price of 31 cents about four weeks ago to 73 percent.
- Sinar Mas clears last major hurdle in takeover of Amcol Holdings, receiving acceptances that would bring interest in Amcol to just over 65 percent, thus making offer unconditional.
- Centrepoint Properties' Causeway Point mall finalising deals with retailers Metro, Marks and Spencer and John Little to be key tenants.
- Lum Chang's mainboard-listed subsidiary LC Development launches prime freehold apartment project in Draycott Park which could gross more than S$125 million if fully sold.
- First Capital Corp buys 14,000 more shares in Sea View Hotel after one-year lapse, bringing stake to 22.86 percent, 2.14 percentage points from takeover trigger point.
- Public offer of Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical Group closes with 8.4 times subscription rate.
